newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse falls as Kenya faces more aid cuts.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse falls as Kenya faces more aid cuts.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index continued to fall on Tuesday after the World Bank said it might follow the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) decision to cut aid to Kenya, bourse officials said.
The index fell a further 11.23 points to 3395.34 points from 3406.57.
But turnover shot up to 27.2 million shillings traded on 496,749 shares from 11.5 million traded on 296,122 shares, due to increased activity by local traders on the Special Boards.
The share index has suffered heavy losses since the IMF announced the lapse of a key aid package on July 31. It stood at 3466.92 on that day just before the news was announced.
Brokers were divided on Tuesday over whether the news that the World Bank may be doing the same has weakened the market further.
"I know two brokers who mainly deal with foreign investors and they cancelled their orders this morning after the World Bank news," a bourse floor trader told Reuters.

A World Bank official said in Washington on Monday the bank had already delaying part of a loan to Kenya and would find it hard to hand over the money until Nairobi addressed concerns on corruption. The official said the bank shared the IMF's concerns.
A broker at a leading trading house said: "Foreign perception is already severely tainted. This news won't create another frenzy."

There was scant activity on the agricultural sector, which accounted for one percent of the day's trades. Rea Vipingo Plantations had 1,000 shares trading hands at 8.5 shillings against 8.7. Brooke Bond and Kakuzi crept up a shilling each to stand at 123 and 111 respectively.

Activity on the commercial sector was brisker, with Uchumi Supermarkets moving 97,053 shares at between 38.25-38.75 shillings. Lonrho Motors East Africa shed three shillings to close at 56, traded on 400 shares.

The lion's share of trading took place in the finance and investment board, totalling 66 percent of the day's trades. ICDC Investments was Tuesday's main feature, trading 242,402 shares at between 62.5 and 70 shillings from 64.

Activity in the bond market heightened, with turnover of the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond shooting up to 295 million shillings from 102 million. The bonds sold at 102.5000 percent from 102.4274 percent.
